memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Moses went out and told the people what the Lord had said. He brought together seventy of their elders and had them stand around the tent. Then the Lord came down in the cloud and spoke with him, and he took some of the power of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied — but did not do so again. — Num 11:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God kept His promise. The seventy elders gathered, the cloud descended, and the Spirit that rested on Moses now rested on them too. As a visible sign, they prophesied — a public confirmation that God had truly equipped them to share the load.

Notice that this prophesying happened once and "did not do so again." The point was not an ongoing dramatic display but a clear, one-time confirmation that these men were genuinely called and empowered. God graciously gave both Moses and the people proof they could see.

This scene is a small foretaste of something far greater. Here the Spirit rests on seventy leaders; but the prophet Joel promised a day when God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh — sons and daughters, young and old, servants and free. That day came at Pentecost, when the Spirit filled all of God's people, not just a chosen few.

If you belong to Christ, the same Spirit who empowered these elders now lives in you. You are not left to serve God in your own strength. Whatever He calls you to do, He equips you to do by His Spirit within you. The work is His, the power is His, and the glory is His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rely on God's Spirit, or on your own strength, to serve Him?
2. What has God called you to that you feel unequipped for?
3. How does the indwelling Spirit change the way you face that calling?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the gift of Your Spirit who equips me to serve. Help me to depend on Your power rather than my own, and to walk each day in step with the Spirit. Amen.
